extracted.intended_audience: Al Jazeera journalists, editors and newsroom staff (global news media professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: A newsroom code of ethics specifying professional standards and behaviours Al Jazeera staff should follow when gathering, producing and presenting news and opinion. Focuses on truth, fairness, diversity, transparency, and colleague/support obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to journalistic values
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the journalistic values of honesty, courage, fairness, balance, independence, credibility and diversity, giving no priority to commercial or political over professional consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endeavour to get to the truth and declare it unequivocally
rubrics_metrics.description: Endeavour to get to the truth and declare it in our dispatches, programmes and news bulletins unequivocally in a manner which leaves no doubt about its validity and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat audiences and victims with respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat our audiences with due respect and address every issue or story with due attention to present a clear, factual and accurate picture while giving full consideration to the feelings of victims of crime, war, persecution and disaster, their relatives and our viewers, and to individual privacies and public decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcome fair competition without compromising standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Welcome fair and honest media competition without allowing it to affect adversely our standards of performance and thereby having a 'scoop' would not become an end in itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not sacrifice professional standards for speed or exclusives; competition is acceptable only if standards remain intact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present diverse points of view without bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the diverse points of view and opinions without bias and partiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise and faithfully reflect societal diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise diversity in human societies with all their races, cultures and beliefs and their values and intrinsic individualities so as to present unbiased and faithful reflection of them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and correct mistakes promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge a mistake when it occurs, promptly correct it and ensure it does not recur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections should be timely and accompanied by measures to prevent repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe transparency with news and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe transparency in dealing with the news and its sources while adhering to the internationally established practices concerning the rights of these sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open about sourcing and methods where appropriate, while respecting source rights and established international practice (e.g., confidentiality protections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between news, opinion and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between news material, opinion and analysis to avoid the snares of speculation and propaganda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label and separate reporting from commentary and analysis to prevent misleading audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support colleagues and defend press freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Stand by colleagues in the profession and give them support when required, particularly in the light of the acts of aggression and harassment to which journalists are subjected at times. Cooperate with Arab and international journalistic unions and associations to defend freedom of the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide practical and institutional support to journalists facing threats; engage with professional bodies to uphold press freedoms.
